An open-source coding model has been released that outperforms Claude Opus 4.7 on key benchmarks

DeepReinforce has released Ornith-1.0, a family of open-source models tailored for agent encoding. There are four variants: 9B Dense, 31B Dense, 35B MoE, and 397B MoE. Based on Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5.

The key idea of the model is that it learns not only to solve tasks but also to build scenarios for their solutions. Conventional models receive a ready-made "framework" of how to approach the task and work with it. Ornith generates and improves it during the training process.

The flagship 397B version scored 77.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 82.4 on SWE-Bench Verified. Claude Opus 4.7 on the same tests shows 70.3 and 80.8.

The 35B version outperforms Qwen 3.5-397B on Terminal-Bench, meaning a model eleven times smaller in parameters works better on this test.

The 9B variant, which runs on regular hardware, outperforms Gemma 4-31B on several benchmarks.

All models are available on Hugging Face.

Good morning from Galilee, Israel.

This is my last Shabbat here in my beloved homeland until nearly the middle of August. In the coming weeks, I’ll have the privilege of spending time with many of you aboard the Alaska cruise and at conferences across America, Dubai, New Zealand, and Australia. My family will be with me for the first part of this journey. After that, I’ll continue - partly on my own and partly with my dear friend, Pastor Barry Stagner.

One would think that after all these years of traveling and speaking around the world, this would come naturally. The truth is - it never does.

Every tour begins with the same three questions.

Am I spiritually ready?

This time I’ll be sharing several brand-new messages on the cruise while also bringing recent teachings to many places I’ve never had the opportunity to visit before.

Am I physically ready?

Over the next seven and a half weeks, I’ll speak 30 times, take 15 flights, and travel thousands of miles. For someone living with a herniated disc, airports and long travel days are anything but enjoyable.

Am I mentally ready?

Different time zones, changing cultures, unfamiliar environments, constant packing and unpacking, changing weather, and the responsibility of ministering day after day can be overwhelming.

The enemy never fails to whisper the same answer to each of those questions:

“No.”

But then the Lord reminds me:

“Have I not commanded you? Be strong and of good courage; do not be afraid, nor be dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”
Joshua 1:9 (NKJV)

“My grace is sufficient for you, for My strength is made perfect in weakness.”
2 Corinthians 12:9 (NKJV)

Scripture also teaches me not to hesitate to ask for your prayers:

“Finally, brethren, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run swiftly and be glorified… and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men; for not all have faith.”
2 Thessalonians 3:1–2 (NKJV)

Thank you for praying - for strength, wisdom, protection, health, safe travels, and above all, that the Messiah would be glorified and His Word would be faithfully proclaimed wherever He opens a door.

Thank you for standing with us.

Awaiting His Return,

Amir

Turkey’s Long Arm, Israel’s Short Patience

Turkey doesn’t need to invade anything to sit inside Israel’s strategic perimeter; it just needs to be everywhere that matters at once. The expert survey on Ankara’s role around Israel reads like a manual for quiet, persistent leverage, not dramatic showdowns.

On the Turkic front, the analysts say Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan are playing hard pragmatism, not romantic pan‑Turkism. Kazakhstan keeps its economic and tech track with Israel and the UAE while doing identity and security business through Turkey and the Organization of Turkic States.

 Baku treats its relationship with Israel as an “existential” security link against Iran that Ankara simply cannot replace. The OTS itself comes off as mostly symbolic — a summit club with thin logistics underneath — while real influence runs through bilateral defense deals, drones, training and intelligence.

Where the alarm really spikes is Gaza and Jerusalem. Across the spectrum, the experts rank Turkey’s ideological and proxy patronage — above all its role as political cover and resource hub for Hamas and Islamist networks — as the top threat vector. A Turkish military contingent in Gaza is seen as a red line with broad consensus inside Israel. 

They see a different kind of threat: a “soft” entry focused on East Jerusalem, the Palestinian Authority and Israel’s Arab society. Humanitarian projects, schools, religious networks and charities become the vehicle — over three to five years — for turning social services into political capital and, eventually, a kind of informal protectorate. The sequence is blunt: aid programs, then education, then mosques and preachers, then community loyalty, and finally leverage over local elites.

On NATO and the U.S. track, the picture is one of structural ambiguity. Turkey uses its veto, its special relationship with Russia and its Islamist clients as bargaining chips, while Washington oscillates between pressure and accommodation. 

The experts warn that Israel cannot count on American discipline to keep Ankara in line and will have to build its own deterrent configuration instead of outsourcing the problem. 

The most likely trajectory to 2030, in their view, is “managed hostility”: embassies at reduced rank, trade rerouted through third countries, constant rhetorical conflict — and a shared, unspoken interest in avoiding a direct break.

❗️ XRP price forms multi-month falling wedge near $1 support as liquidations mount 

📣 According to data from cryptonews price, XRP price dropped from around $1.07 on June 25 to $1.01 on June 26, extending its year-to-date decline to more than 40%. The decline accelerated as a $10.8 billion crypto options expiry triggered heavy volatility across digital assets and forced a wave of long liquidations.

⚠️ At the same time, sentiment surrounding the XRP ecosystem weakened after decentralized finance protocol Strobe Finance abruptly announced it would shut down operations.

🔖 The daily chart shows XRP trading at the lower edge of a falling wedge that has contained price action for almost a year. The pattern has compressed between descending resistance and gradually declining support, with the token now sitting close to the wedge’s lower boundary near $1.00.

🔗 Momentum indicators remain weak. The MACD has stayed below its signal line with histogram bars still in negative territory, while the Aroon indicator continues to favor sellers after Aroon Down climbed back toward 100 and Aroon Up remained subdued.
